title: A gas crosses the membrane
hook: Predict where the cargo ends up, then run the model.

knows: Cells have a plasma membrane separating inside from outside.
doesNotKnow: Oxygen can diffuse across the lipid bilayer. In this equal-volume example, the net movement starts from the higher concentration outside toward the lower concentration inside. The selected four particles illustrate a model, not a prediction for individual trajectories.

misconception: Everything crosses a cell membrane by the same mechanism.
objective: Oxygen can diffuse across the lipid bilayer. In this equal-volume example, the net movement starts from the higher concentration outside toward the lower concentration inside. The selected four particles illustrate a model, not a prediction for individual trajectories.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: A model has more oxygen molecules outside a cell than inside. Oxygen can cross the lipid bilayer. What is the net direction initially? Oxygen can diffuse across the lipid bilayer. In this equal-volume example, the net movement starts from the higher concentration outside toward the lower concentration inside. The selected four particles illustrate a model, not a prediction for individual trajectories.
Recall: Does simple diffusion directly require ATP? Simple diffusion is passive; it does not directly consume ATP.
The diagram is schematic and represents only selected molecules, not trajectories or all particles.
